name: Ultraformer III
lead: Ultraformer III is a Korean high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) device used for noninvasive facial lifting and skin rejuvenation. Clinics use it to tighten loose skin along the jawline, cheeks, neck and around the eyes without incisions, so that the lower face looks firmer and more defined. Published studies in the sources cited here mainly concern the related Ultraformer MPT model, and are listed as such below.[2][3]

HIFU is described as a noninvasive approach to facial rejuvenation reported to promote collagen synthesis and reduce subcutaneous fat.[1] Studies have examined its effects by frequency, by facial aesthetic unit using 3D scanning, and on eyelid sagging.[1][2][3] In looksmaxxing terms it sits among the non-surgical options for jawline and midface tightening, alongside radiofrequency and threads.
infobox: Mild pain and redness reported, resolving in days (eyelid study)[3]

paras: HIFU delivers focused ultrasound energy to skin layers at selected depths; a 2025 study examined how different frequencies affect specific skin layers and correlated histology with patient-reported outcomes.[1]

HIFU devices focus ultrasound energy to a small point beneath the skin so that tissue at the focus is heated while overlying layers are spared. The general medical literature on HIFU, summarised on Wikipedia, describes tissue at the focal point reaching about 65 to 85 degrees Celsius with a focal region a few millimetres deep, with the cosmetic devices using smaller, shallower foci than the cancer and neurological systems described there.[7] In the cosmetic studies cited here, cartridges deliver energy at set depths, such as 2.0 to 6.0 mm in the pig-skin experiment, and the proposed benefits are collagen and elastin synthesis and subcutaneous fat reduction at those depths.[1]

ClinicalTrials.gov lists a 273-participant safety and effectiveness study of a HIFU device for lax submental and neck tissue that started in November 2025, a completed 180-participant study of a HIFU device for eyebrow lifting that started in November 2024, and a small ten-participant trial comparing Ultraformer MPT combined with fractional CO2 laser against fractional CO2 alone for facial rejuvenation.[4][5][6]

A 2024 study of 50 patients used three-dimensional scanning to measure lifting across seven facial aesthetic units after HIFU with Ultraformer MPT.[2] A prospective cohort of 34 Korean women with mild to moderate eyelid laxity received a single HIFU session with Ultraformer MPT and was evaluated for efficacy and safety; its authors note that noticeable improvement in eyelid sagging with noninvasive methods has been challenging.[3] A 2025 histology study compared HIFU frequencies against subjective assessments.[1]

Registered trials include a 273-participant study of a HIFU device for submental and neck laxity, a 180-participant eyebrow-lifting study, and a small trial combining Ultraformer MPT with fractional CO2.[4][5][6]

The 2025 frequency study used two arms. In pig skin treated with Ultraformer MPT at depths of 2.0, 3.0, 4.5 and 6.0 mm, immunohistochemistry and staining showed increased collagen and elastin fibre synthesis and significant fat reduction; in 50 Asian women aged 30 to 60 with skin laxity, clinical outcomes were scored with standardized photographs, the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale and a modified Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale, and 85.3 percent reported overall satisfaction.[1]

The 2024 three-dimensional study measured immediate lifting after treatment with micropulsed cartridges chosen according to sonographic anatomy, reporting lifts of about 1.24 mm at the forehead, 2.25 mm at the crow's feet, 2.46 mm at the malar region, 3.40 mm at the posterior cheek, 2.90 mm at the jowl, 3.09 mm at the mandible and 3.53 mm at the neck.[2] Its authors attribute the smaller forehead lift to thin tissue requiring a cautious approach to avoid discomfort.[2]

In the eyelid study, 34 Korean women aged 31 to 67 received one session with a 2.0 mm, 4 MHz probe delivering 120 shots to the periocular region. At 12 weeks, mean eyelid length had decreased by 0.94 mm, 76 percent of patients reported improvement and clinicians recognised improvement in 59 percent of cases; mild pain and redness were the only side effects, resolving within three to four days.[3]

card.summary: Korean HIFU lifting device; published studies are small and mostly cover the related Ultraformer MPT model.
card.note: Cited studies concern Ultraformer MPT rather than the III specifically.

quick.overview:
Ultraformer III is a Korean HIFU machine used in clinics for non-surgical facial lifting.

Published studies are small cohorts, mostly on the related Ultraformer MPT, covering facial lifting by area, eyelid sagging and ultrasound frequency.
quick.mechanism: Focused ultrasound heats tissue at selected depths, described as promoting collagen synthesis and reducing subcutaneous fat.
quick.risks: Safety details were not available beyond the studies' own safety evaluations; several larger device trials are registered.

chain: Focused ultrasound heats tissue at chosen depths beneath the skin
Collagen remodelling and some fat reduction in the treated layers
Tighter skin and a lifted, more defined jaw and cheek contour
angle.text: Treatment aims to lift sagging tissue along the jowls, cheeks, neck and brow. In published studies on the MPT model, 3D scans showed measurable lift in each facial area and many participants reported satisfaction.
